simulation.assumptions: The designs are stylized: Gaussian shocks, equal cluster sizes, AR(1) persistence, and an exponential spatial covariance. They fix the mechanism, not the magnitude, of each problem
simulation.estimand: For each design and each candidate vcov argument, the probability that a 5% test of the true null (coefficient = 0) rejects, over repeated draws from the design
simulation.estimator: Share of 1,000 independent draws in which fixest's p-value, under that vcov argument and its default small-sample corrections, is below 0.05
simulation.randomness: The design itself: new shocks, new assignment, new regressor in every draw; nothing is sampled from a real population
simulation.target_population: None. Each design is a synthetic data-generating process built so that the source of variation is known; the lab asks which variance estimator describes it
simulation.title: Six designs, one question: how often does a nominal 5% test reject a true null?
simulation.variance_estimator: Monte Carlo: binomial standard error about 0.7% at a true rate of 5%
